speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. To help me understand the issue with your right ring finger, can you describe when the swelling and pain started and if there was any specific injury or bite that preceded it?

speaker: Patient
text: 22-year-old male. The patient reports that the pain and swelling in his right ring finger began 2 days ago while playing football. He recalls his finger got caught in the jersey of another player, who then pulled away forcefully.

speaker: Doctor
text: That sounds like a classic mechanism for a mallet finger or a fracture. Can you actively straighten the tip of your right ring finger against resistance, or does it droop down when you try?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Progressive swelling and pain in the right ring finger. I also have Inability to flex the right ring finger at the distal interphalangeal joint when making a fist, Pain at the distal interphalangeal joint, Extended right ring finger in resting position.

speaker: Doctor
text:
The inability to flex the DIP joint while the finger rests in extension suggests a flexor tendon injury, specifically a flexor digitorum profundus avulsion, often called a "Jersey finger." To confirm this and rule out a fracture, I need to see the anatomy.

REQUEST TEST: X-Ray_right_ring_finger
REQUEST IMAGES

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: X-ray of the Right Hand: No bone fractures or dislocations visible. Soft tissue swelling noted around the distal interphalangeal joint of the right ring finger.

speaker: Doctor
text:
The negative X-ray rules out a fracture, which strongly supports a diagnosis of a Flexor Digitorum Profundus (FDP) avulsion, commonly known as Jersey Finger. This is further confirmed by the mechanism of injury and the inability to flex the DIP joint.

DIAGNOSIS READY: Jersey Finger (Flexor Digitorum Profundus Avulsion)

DIAGNOSIS_READY_Answer: Rupture of the flexor digitorum profundus tendon at its point of insertion
